name: PhyX
intro: PhyX 是面向真实视觉场景物理推理的大规模基准，包含 3,000 个独立问题、6 个物理领域、25 个子领域和 6 种推理类型。每题同时提供开放题与选择题以及 Full-Text、Text-DeRedundancy、Text-Minimal 三种视图，形成 18,000 个核心评测实例。
org: The University of Hong Kong, University of Michigan, Independent Researchers, University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University
build_method: STEM研究生专家采集, OE/MC双题型转换, 三文本视图, 物理博士生三级质控
task_type: 多模态问答, 物理推理
eval_feature: 3,300到3,000筛选, 18,000核心实例, 1,000题testmini, 规则抽取与DeepSeek-V3 Judge
scale: 3,000个独立问题, 6,000个OE/MC问题, 18,000个核心实例, 1,000题testmini
build_method_en: Expert collection by STEM graduate students, paired OE/MC conversion, three text views, three-stage quality control by physics PhD students
eval_feature_en: 3,300-to-3,000 curation, 18,000 core instances, 1,000-problem testmini, rule extraction and DeepSeek-V3 judging
intro_en: PhyX is a large-scale benchmark for physics-grounded reasoning in realistic visual scenarios. It contains 3,000 unique problems across 6 physics domains, 25 subdomains, and 6 reasoning types. Every problem has open-ended and multiple-choice formats plus Full-Text, Text-DeRedundancy, and Text-Minimal views, yielding 18,000 core evaluation instances.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2505.15929, the official PhyX project page, and the official repository. The paper defines a four-stage collection pipeline: survey six physics domains, 25 subdomains, and six reasoning types; recruit STEM graduate annotators under copyright and contamination guidance; convert every item between OE and MC and build Full-Text, Text-DeRedundancy, and Text-Minimal variants; and use GPT-4o to caption images for text-only LLMs. The initial 3,300 candidates undergo lexical-overlap duplicate detection, physics-PhD manual review and scientific validation, and shortest-10-percent filtering to reach 3,000 unique problems and 18,000 core format-view instances. testmini proportionally samples 1,000 problems. Evaluation uses zero-shot CoT generation, rule-based answer extraction, DeepSeek-V3 judging for OE, letter matching with judge fallback for MC, and Accuracy slices by format, view, domain, and reasoning type.
